children: The Czech central bank left the countercyclical capital buffer for banks unchanged after a quarterly review on Thursday, but said that the likelihood of a further increase has risen.

The bank last raised the buffer, one of capital layers that banks must keep to cover risks of losses triggered by various developments or fluctuations in lending, in June by 25 basis points to 1.50%, effective from July 2027.
The bank said this was sufficient for the time being but strong credit growth could change the balance.

"If credit growth and indebtedness in both sectors of the real economy continue to rise and lead to a further movement into the expansionary phase of the financial cycle, the bank board stands ready to increase the countercyclical capital buffer rate further, and the likelihood of such a step has increased," the bank said.
